events.whyItMatters: The procedural blockade around InMode's contested take-private has been lifted: the Haifa District Court threw out Steel Partners affiliate SP Strategic Holdings' request for temporary injunctive relief in its entirety and awarded the company and its directors costs, ending the freeze that had stopped the special committee from choosing between Steel Partners' $16.75-a-share all-cash offer and the CEO-led group's $16.20 bid. The independence challenge that justified the injunction failed, so the decision now returns to the board -- and the open question flips from whether the committee may act to whether a bidding war develops or the insider group prevails.

phases.headline: Steel Partners offers to acquire InMode for $16.75 per share in cash
Haifa court blocks InMode board from deciding between competing buyout bids pending Steel Partners injunction hearing, extends response deadline to July 19
Steel Partners Urges InMode Shareholders to Vote AGAINST the Re-Election of Dr. Hadar Ron and AGAINST Extraordinary Special Committee Compensation at the July 30 Annual General Meeting
InMode: Haifa District Court denied SP Strategic Holdings' request for temporary injunctive relief in its entirety

events.whyItMatters: After three rejections Prologis has a firm Rule 2.7 recommended offer on the table: 0.0920 new Prologis shares for each Segro share, valuing Segro at roughly GBP14.3bn (~$18.8bn) with a partial cash alternative capped at GBP3.5bn -- up to about 1054p a share, a 42% premium to the June 23 unaffected close. It would take one of the FTSE 100's largest REITs off the LSE and hand Prologis a European logistics platform, but the consideration is mostly paper, so Segro holders end up owning Prologis stock, and completion is not expected until the first half of 2027.

phases.headline: Prologis pushes for SEGRO engagement on potential combination
Segro board unanimously rejects Prologis's unsolicited ~886p/share takeover proposal as inadequate
UK's Segro rejects Prologis' $18.2 billion sweetened takeover proposal
Prologis tables 'best and final' £14bn ($18.8bn) takeover proposal for Segro; Segro board signals it is minded to recommend as both sides secure PUSU deadline extension to August 12
Prologis Announces Recommended Acquisition of SEGRO plc
phases.priceReaction: 42% premium to the June 23 unaffected close

events.whyItMatters: Every regulatory condition in the ~$110bn Warner Bros. Discovery merger agreement is now satisfied -- 68 jurisdictions cleared across an eight-month review, with Mexico last on August 14 -- so the antitrust risk that dominated this deal for a year is gone and Paramount says it could close immediately. What is left is purely a US courtroom problem: a 12-state attorneys-general suit led by California holds closing until five days after a 12-day trial starting March 2, 2027, while Paramount owes WBD holders roughly $7m a day from September 30, 2026. The question for holders is no longer whether the deal is permitted but how much the delay costs.

phases.headline: Coalition of 12 states sues to block Paramount Skydance's Warner Bros. Discovery merger
Writers Guild of America sues to block Paramount Skydance-Warner Bros. Discovery merger, alleging the deal will suppress writers' wages and cut job opportunities
Paramount Skydance's $110B merger with Warner Bros. Discovery paused by judge

Paramount Skydance agrees to joint stipulation pausing $111bn Warner Bros. Discovery merger until five days after an antitrust trial or June 1, 2027, whichever is earlier; WGA's preliminary-injunction motion withdrawn as moot

Paramount agrees to pay Warner Bros. Discovery shareholders roughly $7 million per day if the merger remains unclosed after September 30, 2026, as part of the litigation-pause stipulation -- a potential ~$1.7bn cost if the pause runs to the June 1, 2027 outside date
Paramount, Warner Bros. merger challenges set for a 12-day antitrust trial starting March 2, 2027 before US District Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin in Oakland
UK Competition and Markets Authority approves Paramount Skydance Corporation acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery at Phase 1, taking the deal's clearances to 66 jurisdictions
Paramount Skydance Satisfies All Regulatory Conditions Under the Merger Agreement to Close Warner Bros. Discovery Acquisition, Securing Clearances in Nearly 70 Countries Worldwide

events.whyItMatters: The backstop is now firm and sized: Nvidia will provide up to $105bn of credit for the first 4.25GW of the SB Energy-built PORTS-Pike campus in Pike County, Ohio, leased to OpenAI for 20 years, with an option covering a further 3.75GW. That is down from the $250bn covering the whole 10GW project first reported in July, so the balance-sheet exposure is capped at one phase and contingent on the second being taken up. It does not remove the circularity of underwriting your own largest customer -- Nvidia is lending against a campus whose entire compute fit-out it will also supply -- but it converts an open-ended rumoured guarantee into a bounded, disclosed commitment investors can actually underwrite.

phases.headline: Nvidia in talks with OpenAI to guarantee $250 billion financing for data center, WSJ reports
Nvidia scales back $250 billion OpenAI data center guarantee, WSJ reports
Nvidia backing $105 billion in financing for OpenAI data center in Ohio

events.whyItMatters: KKR's $127-a-share, ~$5.7bn all-cash take-private of medical-device contract manufacturer Integer Holdings is now signed and unanimously recommended by the board, resolving the strategic review opened in April 2026 at a 51.8% premium to the unaffected price and a 28.8% premium to the 30-day VWAP. The question shifts from whether a deal happens to whether shareholder and regulatory approvals land by the targeted year-end close -- or whether a topping bid surfaces first.

phases.headline: KKR nearing deal to acquire Integer Holdings, WSJ reports
Integer to Be Acquired by KKR in Transaction Valued at Approximately $5.7 Billion
phases.priceReaction: 51.8% premium to the April 29 unaffected close

events.whyItMatters: SG Fleet Topco -- the Pacific Equity Partners vehicle that took SG Fleet private -- has put an unsolicited, non-binding A$3.60-a-share (~A$760.3m) scheme proposal to FleetPartners, a 27% premium that would put two of Australia's largest fleet-management and novated-leasing books under one private owner. The board has committed to nothing and is evaluating with UBS and Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer, so the open questions are whether it engages at all and whether a combination of this scale clears the ACCC.

phases.headline: Australia's FleetPartners shares on track for best day in 6 years on $534 million takeover bid

events.whyItMatters: Holcim is exiting the Philippines outright -- 68% of its local business goes to China's Huaxin Cement for $527m now, the balance over three to five years for at least $280m, roughly $807m in total -- its largest divestment since the $1bn sale of its Nigeria arm to the same buyer. It continues the redeployment of capital out of emerging-market cement and into higher-multiple building solutions, with completion expected in the first half of 2027.

phases.headline: Holcim to sell Philippines unit to China's Huaxin in $807 million deal

events.whyItMatters: The UK Takeover Panel pushed Castlelake's put-up-or-shut-up deadline out to August 7 to match Apollo's, so both bidders for easyJet must now declare a firm offer or walk away on the same day. easyJet's board has an agreement in principle with Apollo at 715p a share (~GBP5.7bn) and is no longer minded to recommend Castlelake's 690p, which makes Friday binary: either a GBP5.7bn take-private of Europe's second-largest low-cost carrier goes firm, or a two-bidder auction collapses back to a standalone airline.

phases.headline: UK Takeover Panel extends Castlelake's deadline for a firm easyJet offer from August 3 to August 7, aligning it with Apollo's deadline
Apollo agrees to buy UK airline EasyJet in $7.7 billion deal as Castlelake withdraws
phases.priceReaction: 81% premium to the GBP3.94 unaffected close

events.whyItMatters: Prysmian pays $95 a share in cash (~$3.8bn enterprise value, a 30% premium to Atkore's July 31 close) to buy a US maker of electrical conduit, cable management and metal framing -- the step that turns the world's largest cable manufacturer into a broader electrical-solutions supplier into North American data centres and grid build-out. It targets $150m of annual synergies by 2029 and earnings accretion from year one, and it ends the strategic review Atkore opened in September 2025 at a ~57% premium to the pre-review price.

phases.headline: Prysmian Strikes Deal to Buy US Electrical Maker Atkore for $95.00 per Share in Cash

events.whyItMatters: Supernus and Indivior combine in a tax-free all-stock merger of equals -- 1.5401 Indivior shares per Supernus share, leaving Indivior holders with ~56.5% and Supernus holders ~43.5% of a ~$2.2bn-revenue CNS biopharma listed on Nasdaq as SUPN -- with $125m of expected annual cost synergies and a $1bn pre-closing special cash dividend to Indivior investors part-funded by a $650m Citibank term loan. It is a scale answer to both companies' single-franchise concentration risk, but the debt-funded special dividend means the combined balance sheet starts levered.

phases.headline: Supernus Pharmaceuticals and Indivior Pharmaceuticals to Merge, Creating a Diversified CNS Biopharmaceutical Leader with Significant Scale

events.counterparty: Public Investment Fund (with Silver Lake, Affinity Partners)
events.whyItMatters: The largest leveraged buyout on record closes: EA leaves the Nasdaq after 37 years at $210 a share in cash (a 25% premium to its $168.32 unaffected price), funded with ~$36bn of equity and ~$20bn of JPMorgan-committed debt, leaving Saudi Arabia's PIF with 93.4%, Silver Lake 5.5% and Affinity Partners 1.1%. It removes a $55bn name from public markets, sets a new ceiling for what sponsor-plus-sovereign capital can take private, and puts a major Western games publisher under majority state ownership.

phases.headline: Electronic Arts completes $55 billion take-private by PIF, Silver Lake and Affinity Partners, the largest leveraged buyout ever

events.whyItMatters: IonQ closes its ~$1.8bn purchase of semiconductor foundry SkyWater Technology after the FTC cleared it without conditions, over the chairman's push to impose fair-access commitments to rival quantum firms that hold SkyWater contracts. It makes IonQ a vertically integrated quantum company that owns its own fab rather than renting capacity -- and hands it control of a chokepoint several competitors depend on.

phases.headline: IonQ closes $1.8bn SkyWater acquisition after US FTC clearance

events.whyItMatters: Resideo completes the spin-off of ADI Global Distribution, distributing one ADI share for every two Resideo shares to holders of record on July 20 and listing ADI on the NYSE as ADIG from August 4. It splits the company into a products business and a distribution business that investors can now value separately -- removing the conglomerate discount, but also removing ADI's revenue scale from the Resideo that remains.

phases.headline: Resideo completes spin-off of ADI Global Distribution; ADI to begin trading on the NYSE as 'ADIG' on August 4

events.whyItMatters: Curium's up-to-$8bn purchase of Lantheus combines two of the largest radiopharmaceutical businesses and takes Lantheus off the Nasdaq, but only $102.50 a share is cash at closing -- the remaining $12.00 sits in non-transferable CVRs tied to prostate-cancer and neurology diagnostic and DEFINITY sales milestones through 2030, so holders reach the headline $114.50 only if the combined franchise delivers. Closing is not expected until the first half of 2027.

phases.headline: Curium Announces Definitive Agreement to Merge with Lantheus

events.whyItMatters: Procter & Gamble pays $3.8bn in cash for science-backed supplements maker Thorne, its biggest push yet into the vitamins, minerals and supplements market and a bolt-on to a health portfolio that already includes New Chapter, Metamucil and Align. It also hands seller L Catterton a return of more than $3bn on the roughly $680m it paid in 2023 -- a reminder that P&G is buying at the top of a wellness cycle rather than early into one. Closing is expected later in 2026, subject to regulatory clearance.

phases.headline: Procter & Gamble will acquire supplements brand Thorne for $3.8 billion, CEO tells CNBC

events.whyItMatters: Both shareholder bases have now approved the all-stock merger of equals between Axalta and AkzoNobel -- 0.6539 AkzoNobel shares per Axalta share, leaving AkzoNobel holders with ~55% and Axalta holders ~45% of a coatings group with ~$17bn of revenue, ~$3.3bn of adjusted EBITDA and $600m of targeted pre-tax run-rate synergies (90% inside three years). The vote removes the shareholder-approval risk that had hung over the deal since the governance terms were revised on July 23; what remains is regulatory clearance and a EUR2.5bn pre-completion distribution condition, with closing guided to late 2026 or early 2027.

phases.headline: Axalta Shareholders Approve Proposed Merger of Equals with AkzoNobel

events.whyItMatters: SpaceX and NVIDIA will jointly design the compute payload for the Starmind AI1 satellite -- NVIDIA Rubin GPUs and Vera CPUs running datacenter-class AI workloads in low Earth orbit -- and Musk used SpaceX's first post-IPO earnings call to say SpaceX will build its AI infrastructure exclusively on NVIDIA going forward, against an eventual ambition of up to a million satellites. It gives NVIDIA an exclusive lock on a brand-new compute frontier and a customer with its own launch capacity, and it closes off SpaceX as a market for rival accelerators; AMD fell on the same news.

phases.headline: SpaceX Commits Exclusively to Nvidia, Unveils Starmind: AMD Falls 9% on Record Quarter

events.whyItMatters: A five-year patent cross-license ends every pending Netlist-Samsung dispute and converts a litigation lottery ticket into contracted cash: $239m upfront (net of Korean withholding tax) plus quarterly fees of up to $32.9m across twenty quarters, up to ~$897m gross in total. It also comes with a supply agreement letting Netlist buy up to $300m of Samsung DRAM and NAND a year (up to $1.5bn over the term) and a 10m-share equity purchase by Samsung under a five-year lock-up. For a company whose equity story was previously a binary bet on court outcomes, that is a different business.

phases.headline: Netlist, Samsung Reach Multi-Million Dollar Memory Tech Deal
phases.priceReaction: +46.5% to $3.75, biggest one-day gain in five years

events.whyItMatters: The largest pharma combination ever floated -- a roughly $400bn AstraZeneca/Bristol Myers Squibb merger reported by the FT and Bloomberg as exploratory -- has been flatly denied by a senior source close to the matter, who told Reuters there never was a deal to be done and no discussions are under way. Neither company has commented on the record either way, so the practical read is that the premium the market briefly priced into BMY and the 7% discount it applied to AZN both rested on a combination that is not being pursued; the antitrust overlap in oncology that made it hard remains the reason it stays unlikely.

phases.headline: AstraZeneca in talks with Bristol Myers Squibb on $400 billion megadeal, FT reports
No deal between AstraZeneca and BMS, senior source insists: "There is no deal between AstraZeneca and BMS. There never was a deal to be done, and there are no discussions between the companies"

events.whyItMatters: Nielsen pays $13.60 a share in cash -- roughly $2.15bn of enterprise value, a 30% premium to DoubleVerify's 60-day VWAP -- to take the ad-verification firm private and bolt media-quality measurement onto its own audience-measurement franchise, targeting a combined business with more than $4bn of annual revenue. It removes one of the few remaining listed pure-play ad-tech names from the Nasdaq and hands a private-equity-owned Nielsen an end-to-end measurement stack, but it is funded with committed debt from Barclays, BofA and Citi plus incremental equity, so the combined entity starts levered. Closing is not expected until the first quarter of 2027.

phases.headline: Nielsen to Acquire DoubleVerify, Creating a Leading, Independent Media Intelligence Platform

events.whyItMatters: Deutsche Telekom more than doubles its 2026 buyback envelope from EUR2bn to as much as EUR5bn and lifts full-year free cash flow guidance to around EUR20bn after a core-earnings beat -- management explicitly framing the increase as a response to the shares' depressed valuation rather than a routine top-up. For a DAX heavyweight that has historically prioritised deleveraging and dividends, committing an extra EUR3bn to repurchases is a genuine shift in how the cash gets returned.

phases.headline: Deutsche Telekom Raises 2026 Share Buyback By Up to EUR3 Billion

events.whyItMatters: Williams buys all of Momentum Midstream for up to $5.5bn -- about $3.5bn of cash and debt plus roughly $2bn of Williams equity, at an implied ~8.5x 2027 EBITDA -- adding more than 4,000 miles of Haynesville gathering pipe, over 1m dedicated acres and three take-or-pay pipelines that move gas toward Gulf Coast LNG and power demand. Paired with the $1.5bn Delta Access project and the Shelby Trough Connector, it is a large, part-equity-funded bet that Haynesville-to-Gulf takeaway is where the LNG and data-center load actually shows up.

phases.headline: Williams Delivers Strong Second-Quarter 2026 Results; Announces Strategic Acquisition of Momentum Midstream Connecting Haynesville to Gulf Coast LNG and Power Demand

events.whyItMatters: Diamondback's board doubles the share-repurchase authorization to $16bn from $8bn, leaving ~$9.9bn available, alongside raised 2026 guidance of 522+ MBO/d of oil and 1,000+ MBOE/d total after crossing the million-barrel-equivalent mark. Doubling the buyback rather than the dividend or the drilling budget is a statement that management sees its own equity as the best use of Permian free cash flow at current strip prices.

phases.headline: Diamondback Energy, Inc. Announces Second Quarter 2026 Financial and Operating Results; Board doubles share repurchase authorization to $16.0 billion

events.whyItMatters: Driven Brands' board unanimously rejects an unsolicited $18.00-a-share all-cash proposal from activist holder ADW Capital -- a 41% premium to the $12.74 close and 42% to the 30-day VWAP -- calling it highly conditional and without a credible basis to proceed. ADW's stated thesis is that the 4,200-location car-wash and auto-services group is cheap because of self-inflicted structural, capital-allocation and governance failures, so the rejection converts a valuation argument into a public pressure campaign that now hangs over the shares whether or not financing ever materialises.

phases.headline: Driven Brands Holdings Inc. Rejects Non-Binding, Highly Conditional and Unsolicited Proposal from ADW Capital

events.whyItMatters: Dream Finders pays $33.50 a share in cash -- about $915m of equity and roughly $2.2bn of enterprise value including assumed debt -- for Beazer Homes, creating the sixth-largest US homebuilder at around 13,000 annual closings and adding Indianapolis, Las Vegas, Sacramento, southern California and Delaware to its map. It ends a months-long pursuit that began with a private offer in February and several rejections, and targets more than $100m of annual run-rate cost synergies. The bet is that scale beats caution: this is debt-assisted consolidation placed into a soft housing market, with closing guided to Q4 2026 subject to Beazer shareholder and regulatory approval.

phases.headline: Dream Finders Homes to Acquire Beazer Homes, Creating Sixth-Largest U.S. Homebuilder

events.whyItMatters: Kirin pays C$45.75 a share in cash for Jamieson Wellness -- about C$2.0bn of fully diluted equity and C$2.5bn of enterprise value, a 27% premium to the 20-day and 32% to the 60-day VWAP to June 24 -- taking the top-share brand in Canada's vitamins, minerals and supplements market off the TSX and giving the Japanese brewer a full-scale North American health platform rather than a beachhead. It is the second large supplements deal in under a week after P&G's $3.8bn purchase of Thorne, which says more about where consumer-staples capital is going than about either buyer. Closing is guided to Q4 2026, subject to a September shareholder vote plus court and regulatory approvals.

phases.headline: Jamieson Wellness Enters into Definitive Agreement to be Acquired by Kirin in C$2.5 Billion Transaction
phases.priceReaction: 27% premium to the 20-day VWAP to June 24

events.counterparty: Oaktree Capital Management, SFS Group Capital (Ishbia family)
events.whyItMatters: UWM raises $2.05bn of permanent capital from Oaktree and the Ishbia family's new SFS Group Capital vehicle -- 1.5m Series A-1 and 150,000 Series A-2 preferred shares at a $1,000 stated value paying 10% in cash or 13% accreted, plus 330m warrants -- and suspends its common dividend to repay debt and MSR financing facilities, with a $400m rights offering held in reserve. It lands alongside a $451.9m second-quarter loss, equity nearly halved to $985.3m and non-funding leverage more than tripled to 6.13x, so this is a balance-sheet rescue with heavy dilution attached rather than an opportunistic raise. The market read it that way: the shares fell about 35%.

phases.headline: UWM Holdings Corporation Announces $2.05 Billion Strategic Capital Partnership with the Ishbia Family and Oaktree

events.whyItMatters: Thyssenkrupp shareholders approved, with 99.99% of votes at an extraordinary general meeting, the spin-off of 49% of tk accelis -- the materials trading arm with roughly 15,500 staff and about EUR11.4bn of sales, its largest division by revenue and valued near EUR3.6bn by Jefferies -- clearing the way for a separate Frankfurt listing as soon as end-October with Thyssenkrupp retaining majority control. It is the third carve-out under the ACES 2030 plan after hydrogen and defence, converting the conglomerate into a holding company and giving investors a directly priceable distribution business; the steel division, where a spin-off or IPO is still only being explored, remains the unresolved piece.

phases.headline: Thyssenkrupp owners approve materials spinoff in latest restructuring move

events.whyItMatters: Delaware's Court of Chancery has invalidated Verisk's December termination of its $2.35bn purchase of roofing-software provider AccuLynx, finding that Verisk's own willful conduct caused the closing condition to fail, ordering it to attempt to complete the deal and entitling AccuLynx to recover its direct costs plus interest. It revives an acquisition Verisk wrote off more than seven months ago and puts a specific-performance obligation back on the buyer -- but the court compelled effort, not an outcome: completion still depends on an FTC review that has never finished.

phases.headline: Delaware judge orders Verisk to proceed with $2.35 billion AccuLynx deal

events.whyItMatters: Diageo commits $1.2bn of restructuring spend to take out roughly $1bn of annual cost -- $850m from a new operating framework landing across fiscal 2027 and 2028, plus $150m from supply-chain work -- after organic net sales fell 2% on weakness in North America and Asia Pacific. Fiscal 2026 already absorbed $0.9bn of restructuring charges, so this is a funded rebuild of the operating model by a new CEO rather than a cost-discipline gesture, and investors treated the savings plan, not the results, as the news.

phases.headline: Diageo unveils $1.2bn restructuring plan as sales decline hits North America and Asia Pacific
phases.priceReaction: shares surged as the $1bn cost-saving plan outweighed weaker annual results

events.whyItMatters: CVC's up-to-915p-a-share cash proposal values Bodycote at about GBP1.56bn and puts the FTSE 250's dominant thermal-processing specialist -- an asset-heavy franchise serving aerospace, autos and energy with no listed pure-play peer -- into a live two-sponsor auction decided by a single penny. The board has said it would recommend either proposal and has opened confirmatory due diligence to both, so the open question for holders is no longer whether Bodycote leaves the LSE but which sponsor firms up by the 2 September Rule 2.6 deadline.

phases.headline: Bodycote confirms a possible cash offer from CVC Advisers of up to 915p a share (907.8p cash plus a 7.2p permitted interim dividend), valuing it at ~GBP1.56bn, and grants confirmatory due diligence ahead of a 2 September Rule 2.6 deadline

events.whyItMatters: Veritas Capital's up-to-914p-a-share proposal sits one penny below CVC's for the same GBP1.56bn asset, which is what makes this a genuine auction rather than a single-bidder approach: Bodycote's board is running both parties through confirmatory due diligence separately and on an expedited basis, and either bid would be recommended. For Veritas the prize is the largest independent heat-treatment and specialist-technology network in the West; for holders, the 1p spread means the outcome turns on which sponsor moves first before 2 September rather than on price alone.

phases.headline: Bodycote confirms a competing possible cash offer from Veritas Capital of up to 914p a share (906.8p cash plus a 7.2p permitted interim dividend), with the board prepared to recommend either proposal

events.whyItMatters: ContextLogic is completing its conversion from the wound-down Wish marketplace into a holding company that parks cash-generative industrials behind a large tax-loss shield: gChem is its second operating business after US Salt. The $850m cash price is funded partly by a $650m rights offering at the public-company level, fully backstopped at $9.00 a unit by a consortium led by Abrams Capital and BC Partners, so existing holders either write a cheque or watch the sponsors' ownership concentrate. Management guides the combined businesses to roughly $95-105m of free cash flow in 2027.

phases.headline: ContextLogic to Acquire gChem for $850 Million, funded in part by a $650m rights offering fully backstopped at $9.00 per unit by a consortium led by Abrams Capital and BC Partners

events.whyItMatters: ENEOS is buying scale in US petrochemicals rather than shrinking alongside Japanese domestic fuel demand: TPC is North America's largest independent C4 hydrocarbon processor and the region's butadiene share leader, and the ~$1.3bn enterprise value brings Houston petrochemical operations plus terminals at Port Neches, Texas and Lake Charles, Louisiana. The deal lifts the ENEOS Group to the world's third-largest butadiene capacity and moves refining cash flow into a feedstock-advantaged Gulf Coast platform, with closing targeted for October 2026.

phases.headline: TPC Group to Be Acquired by ENEOS Holdings at approximately $1.3bn enterprise value, giving the ENEOS Group the world's third-largest butadiene production capacity

events.whyItMatters: Bernhard Capital pays $43.00 a share in cash -- about $1.0bn of enterprise value and a 58% premium to Bowman's unaffected August 7 close -- to take the engineering and infrastructure consultancy off the Nasdaq, backed by $605m of committed BCP equity and $550m of committed debt across term loan, revolver and delayed-draw facilities. It is the second listed engineering consultancy put in play inside a fortnight after WSP's rejected approaches for Arcadis, and the go-shop running to September 13 leaves the door open to a topping bid before the Q4 2026/Q1 2027 close.

phases.headline: Bowman Consulting Group Enters into Definitive Agreement to be Acquired by Bernhard Capital Partners for $43.00 Per Share in Cash
phases.priceReaction: 58% premium to the August 7 unaffected close

events.whyItMatters: Blackstone Infrastructure's Safe Harbor pays $53.00 a share in cash -- roughly $1.5bn of enterprise value and a 96% premium to MarineMax's January 30 unaffected close, 110% to the 90-day VWAP -- ending a six-month process that began with an unsolicited approach. It takes the largest listed US recreational-boating retailer private at a weak point in the marine cycle and hands Safe Harbor 65 marinas and storage sites plus 70 dealerships, its biggest deal since Blackstone bought it for $5.7bn in 2025. The offer is not financing-contingent, so what remains is shareholder and regulatory approval before the targeted end-2026 close.

phases.headline: MarineMax Enters into Definitive Agreement to be Acquired by Blackstone Infrastructure Portfolio Company, Safe Harbor, in a $1.5 Billion All-Cash Transaction
phases.priceReaction: 96% premium to the January 30 unaffected close; shares surged on the report

events.whyItMatters: Teledyne pays $18.90 a share in cash -- about $1.1bn including Varex's net debt and equity awards, at roughly an 88% premium -- for the largest independent maker of X-ray tubes and flat-panel detectors. It moves Teledyne from imaging sensors into the medical-imaging component supply chain and removes one of the few listed pure-play suppliers of next-generation CT detectors from the market. Closing is targeted for early 2027.

phases.headline: Teledyne to Acquire Varex Imaging Corporation

events.whyItMatters: Archer buys Boeing's Wisk Aero, Insitu and SkyGrid entirely in stock -- Boeing receives newly issued shares equal to 19.75% of Archer's pre-closing count, about 16.5% after closing, plus a board nominee -- absorbing its main autonomous-eVTOL rival and picking up in Insitu a defence drone business with more than $200m of annual revenue. For a pre-revenue eVTOL developer that converts dilution into an operating defence franchise and Boeing as an anchor holder; for Boeing it is another non-core disposal that costs no cash while keeping access to Wisk's autonomy stack through a separate collaboration. Closing is expected by end-2026, subject to antitrust review.

phases.headline: Archer to Shape Physical AI Future of Aerospace and Defense with Acquisition of Boeing's Wisk Aero, Insitu and SkyGrid Subsidiaries; Boeing to Invest in Archer and Collaborate

events.whyItMatters: Intel's $15bn underwritten common-stock offering -- its first public share sale since listing in 1971, with a $2.25bn underwriter option on top -- funds capital expenditure management has already guided up to about $20bn for 2026 and 'meaningfully' higher in 2027. Choosing equity over debt protects the balance sheet and the investment-grade rating, but it places the cost of the AI and foundry build-out on existing holders through dilution rather than on lenders, and the market read it that way.

phases.headline: Intel Announces Proposed $15 Billion Common Stock Offering

events.whyItMatters: Bloomberg reports Ryan Cohen is weighing pulling GameStop's $56bn unsolicited bid for eBay -- rejected in May as 'neither credible nor attractive' -- in favour of a partnership or joint venture that would put eBay's trading-card and collectibles business into GameStop's roughly 1,600 US stores, with GameStop seeking a board seat off the back of the stake it already owns. GameStop is down about 28% and eBay up 7.6% since the proposal surfaced, so the arithmetic that made the bid arguable has gone; no decision has been made and this is sourced reporting, not an announcement.

phases.headline: GameStop's Ryan Cohen Weighs Pulling $56 Billion EBay Offer

events.whyItMatters: Tabcorp agrees to buy wagering-technology supplier BetMakers at A$0.24 a share (~A$283m) by scheme of arrangement, unanimously recommended by the BetMakers board, six months after informal talks between the two collapsed in February. It brings in-house the platform Tabcorp needs to modernise its own wagering stack plus an international B2B business, and targets A$30m of annual cost savings by the end of year two -- material for a company of Tabcorp's size. Completion is guided to the third quarter of Tabcorp's FY2027, subject to BetMakers shareholder, court, ACCC and gaming-regulator approvals.

phases.headline: Tabcorp to acquire BetMakers in A$283 million deal, unanimously recommended by the BetMakers board

events.counterparty: Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, KKR
events.whyItMatters: Memorandums of understanding with six of the largest pools of private capital create dedicated compute-financing platforms intended to mobilise more than $500bn of third-party money, with NVIDIA GPUs treated as collateral for debt issued by special-purpose vehicles -- Goldman Sachs leading public offerings and the five alternative managers deploying long-duration institutional and insurance capital. It industrialises the vendor-financing model behind the OpenAI backstop while moving the credit exposure off NVIDIA's own balance sheet onto other people's, and it turns GPU-backed paper into a new asset class; BlackRock's Larry Fink compared it to the creation of mortgage-backed securities. The circularity risk does not disappear, it just gets syndicated.

phases.headline: NVIDIA Partners With Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to Establish AI Compute Infrastructure Financing Platforms to Mobilize Over $500 Billion of Third-Party Capital

events.whyItMatters: Sony and TSMC will put a combined JPY747bn (~$4.7bn) into Advanced Vision Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp in Kumamoto -- Sony JPY465bn (~$2.92bn) in cash and assets including its newly built local fab for 60% and control, TSMC JPY282bn (~$1.77bn) for 40% -- to build next-generation smartphone image sensors alongside TSMC's existing JASM plant. It hands Sony's dominant sensor franchise access to TSMC's advanced logic and shares the capex on a fab Sony would otherwise have carried alone, but the venture consolidates into Sony's accounts and volume production does not start until 2029, so the cost lands years before the revenue.

phases.headline: Sony Semiconductor Solutions and TSMC Agreed to Establish Joint Venture for Next-Generation Image Sensors

events.whyItMatters: Bending Spoons' first deal since its July 1 Nasdaq listing is an all-cash purchase of Airtable at $1.285bn enterprise value, about $2.25bn of implied equity value once Airtable's net cash is counted -- a steep discount to the roughly $11bn the no-code database platform was privately valued at in 2021, for a business with about $480m of ARR still growing north of 20%. It is the buy-mature-software-and-run-it-harder playbook that built the company, now executed for the first time under public-market scrutiny and at a size where the integration matters; closing is expected before year-end subject to regulatory review.

phases.headline: Bending Spoons has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Airtable for $1.285 billion

events.whyItMatters: Sandisk's board adds a $14bn repurchase authorization on top of the $6bn approved in April -- of which roughly $4.5bn was already spent in about two months -- taking remaining capacity to ~$15.5bn, or close to 9% of the company, funded from operating cash flow. It follows a fiscal fourth quarter of $8.97bn revenue and a full year of $20.2bn on AI data-center memory demand, and it is a clear statement of where the windfall goes: back to shareholders at current prices rather than into pre-funding the next capacity cycle, which only works if this memory upcycle holds.

phases.headline: Sandisk board of directors approves a $14 billion share repurchase program, taking total remaining authorization to $15.5 billion

events.counterparty: Trian Fund Management (with BlueFive Capital, Flynn Group)
events.whyItMatters: Trian, Wendy's largest shareholder at about 16%, is assembling co-investors -- BlueFive Capital and Flynn Group, one of the chain's biggest franchisees -- behind a bid to take the burger chain private, days after a sixth consecutive quarter of same-store sales declines. Nelson Peltz has sat on or around this board since 2008, so an insider-led buyout of a roughly $1.4bn-equity franchise business would move the turnaround out of public view at a low point in the cycle. Nothing has been submitted: the company has only said it would review any proposal consistent with its fiduciary duties, and the report is single-sourced with no price attached.

phases.headline: Wendy's stock jumps on report of potential takeover bid from Nelson Peltz's Trian Fund Management
phases.priceReaction: up as much as 16% intraday, biggest gain since June 25

events.whyItMatters: Curaleaf has stopped asking and formally commenced its hostile offer, mailing the bid circular and inviting Aurora holders to tender 0.3463 Curaleaf subordinate voting shares plus US$0.75 cash per share -- an implied US$4.00, about US$260m in total, a 45% premium to Aurora's 30-day VWAP and subject to a US$5.00 cap price -- with the offer open until 5:00 p.m. Mountain Time on December 1, 2026. That takes the outcome out of the boardroom and puts it in the hands of the shareholder register for three and a half months. Aurora's special committee has told holders to take no action for now and accused Curaleaf of pressuring shareholders, so the question is whether a defence or a rival bid arrives before the register decides for itself; the underlying argument has not changed -- Curaleaf is bidding for a cash pile plus an international medical footprint, a 110% premium once Aurora's balance-sheet cash is stripped out.

phases.headline: Curaleaf to take offer directly to shareholders in bid to buy Edmonton-based Aurora Cannabis
Curaleaf Launches Take-Over Bid to Acquire Aurora Cannabis, Invites Aurora Shareholders to Tender to the Bid

events.whyItMatters: Bank of America commits up to INR18,268 crore (~$2.1bn) for 26.5% of Jio Credit at signing, rising to 49.9% if the warrants are exercised -- converting Reliance's two-year-old lending arm, already at INR30,667 crore of assets under management, from a wholly-owned subsidiary into a joint venture with a global bank. For Jio Financial it brings outside capital and underwriting expertise it would otherwise have had to build alone; for BofA it is a first direct balance-sheet position in Indian consumer credit, immaterial against group capital but a real change in where it competes. Regulatory and statutory approvals are still outstanding.

phases.headline: Bank of America Enters into a Joint Venture Agreement with Jio Financial Services Limited to Acquire up to 49.9% in Jio Credit Limited

events.whyItMatters: Reuters reports Silver Lake has held months of talks to take Workday private, which at a ~$43bn market value would rank among the largest software buyouts ever attempted and would need additional co-investors plus a debt package no sponsor has raised for a business of this size in years. For holders the read-across is that the market is now pricing profitable, slow-growing enterprise SaaS at levels where private equity thinks it can clear a return -- but the talks are ongoing, sourced rather than announced, and neither side has confirmed a price.

phases.headline: Exclusive-Silver Lake in talks to buy Workday, sources say
phases.priceReaction: up as much as 25% before trading was halted for volatility; best single day in 10 years

events.whyItMatters: Thoma Bravo pays $20.25 a share in cash -- more than $4bn of enterprise value and a 49% premium to the August 12 close -- to take specialty insurance marketplace Accelerant private barely a year after its NYSE listing, with Altamont Capital Partners' ~82% of the voting rights already committed in favour. That block makes shareholder approval a formality and moves the risk entirely to insurance-regulatory clearance, which the parties have priced explicitly: a 6% annual ticking fee accrues to holders if those approvals delay the close beyond the first half of 2027.

phases.headline: Accelerant Enters into Definitive Agreement to be Acquired by Thoma Bravo
phases.priceReaction: +43% premarket to $19.45; 49% premium to the August 12 close

events.whyItMatters: Dynatrace pays $915m -- roughly $815m in cash from its balance sheet and credit facility, the rest in replacement equity for Arize staff -- to buy the leading independent AI-observability platform and extend its monitoring franchise from infrastructure into how AI models are evaluated and improved in production. It is a bet that observability spend follows workloads into the AI stack rather than being displaced by it, and at a size Dynatrace can fund without new debt; closing is guided to this quarter or early next, subject to regulatory review.

phases.headline: Dynatrace to Acquire AI Observability Leader Arize

events.whyItMatters: Western Union's roughly $500m purchase of Intermex has cleared the New York Department of Financial Services, with Western Union giving commitments on remittance services and locations in the state -- but the same disclosure revealed that California's DFPI had, a day earlier, suspended the approval extension it granted on July 31. Intermex shares jumped because the deal has now cleared most of its regulatory path; the open question is no longer whether the acquisition is agreed but whether a single state regulator lets it close.

phases.headline: Western Union and Intermex Provide Update on Pending Acquisition: New York DFS approval granted, while California's DFPI suspends the approval extension issued on July 31

events.whyItMatters: The three partners have finalised the joint venture and taken final investment decision on a 1,300-mile refined-products system worth about $5bn of enterprise value, connecting St. Louis and expanded Gulf Coast supply points to Arizona and California -- Phillips 66 contributing roughly $2.5bn for 49.9%, Kinder Morgan about $250m for 35.1% and HF Sinclair about $750m for 15%. It is underpinned primarily by 10-year take-or-pay contracts, so the revenue is contracted rather than merchant, but completion is targeted for 2029 and the permits are not yet secured, meaning the capital goes out years ahead of the cash coming back.

phases.headline: Phillips 66, Kinder Morgan and HF Sinclair Announce Final Investment Decision for Western Gateway Pipeline

events.whyItMatters: Goldman Sachs pays as much as $2.25bn in cash and equity, part of it contingent on performance and service milestones, for a manager of 19 options-based income ETFs with about $30bn of assets at June 30 -- buying a derivative-income product line, including the NEOS Bitcoin High Income, Boosted Bitcoin High Income and Ethereum High Income ETFs, rather than building one. It is a bet that advisor and retail demand for options-overlay income keeps compounding, and it hands Goldman Sachs Asset Management a crypto-income ETF franchise it has no organic equivalent to.

phases.headline: Goldman Sachs Announces Agreement to Acquire NEOS Investments

events.whyItMatters: SpaceX has closed the largest acquisition of a private startup on record, issuing 389,289,254 Class A shares -- plus 1,752,426 more for vested RSUs and roughly 29.1m assumed RSUs and 44.4m options -- for Cursor maker Anysphere at a $60bn implied equity value, struck on the seven-day VWAP into closing. It is paid entirely in paper, so existing holders fund an AI coding-tools business out of their own dilution barely six weeks after the Nasdaq listing, and Cursor becomes a wholly owned unit of a new SpaceXAI division. The case now rests on whether an AI software franchise can be run inside a launch and satellite company, because the shares have already been spent.

phases.headline: SpaceX completes acquisition of Anysphere in $60 billion all-stock deal

events.whyItMatters: Both shareholder bases have now cleared Real's roughly $880m purchase of RE/MAX -- 99.0% of Real votes cast in favour and holders of 78.8% of RE/MAX voting power -- leaving a final order from the Supreme Court of British Columbia as effectively the last step before the two list as Real REMAX Group. RE/MAX holders elect $13.80 a share in cash or 5.152 Real REMAX shares, with aggregate cash capped between $60m and $80m, so almost the entire consideration is stock: they end up owning about 41% of a technology-led brokerage rather than cashing out of a franchise brand, and the value of what they received depends on an integration that has not started.

phases.headline: Real and RE/MAX Holdings Securityholders Approve Proposed Combination

events.whyItMatters: Core Scientific paid roughly $444m in cash -- above the ~$421m it signed for in May -- to buy a rival miner's campus outright, and what it actually bought is ~440MW of in-service, grid-connected capacity under existing Oklahoma Gas & Electric service agreements. That is the scarce input in the AI build-out: energised interconnect, not land. It takes the Muskogee campus toward 1.5GW of gross power and continues the conversion of former bitcoin-mining sites in Texas, Georgia, North Carolina and Oklahoma into high-density AI colocation, moving the revenue base off hash-price beta and onto contracted compute leases.

phases.headline: Core Scientific Completes Acquisition of Polaris DS, Advancing Muskogee Expansion to 1.5 Gigawatts of Gross Power

events.whyItMatters: Nvidia is putting $1.5bn of equity into the developer building OpenAI's Ohio campus and, in exchange, locks in sole-supplier status for the compute infrastructure on a site that scales from 4.25GW to 8GW -- plus access to that capacity for its own use. Pairing an equity stake in the landlord with up to $105bn of credit to the project moves Nvidia from chip vendor to part-owner of the power and real estate layer, which is where AI supply is actually constrained: SB Energy and SoftBank plan at least 10GW of new generation, a 9.2GW on-site gas plant costing ~$33bn, and $4.2bn into Ohio grid infrastructure. It also deepens the circular-financing exposure critics are already pricing into the name.

phases.headline: Nvidia to invest $1.5 billion in SB Energy under OpenAI data center deal

events.whyItMatters: TTM is paying $1.1bn cash -- funded entirely with new senior secured term loans from JPMorgan, Barclays and Bank of America -- to buy a defence electronics business, taking net leverage to ~2.3x at closing on a company that has spent years de-levering. What it buys is a move up the value chain from printed circuit boards into AI-enabled software-defined radios, RF products and radiation-tolerant space compute, lifting exposure to missile defence, signals intelligence, electronic warfare and space. Management guides to immediate adjusted-EBITDA margin accretion but non-GAAP EPS accretion only in 2028, and the market marked the stock down on announcement: the integration and the debt come first, the earnings later.

phases.headline: TTM Technologies, Inc. Continues Global Growth Strategy with Planned Acquisition of Epiq Solutions, Enhancing Technologically Differentiated Market Offerings

events.whyItMatters: Alibaba has agreed to sell its entire stake in game developer Lingxi Games to Trustar Capital for more than $2bn, roughly double the RMB7-9bn the unit was valued at when the sale was first floated in June. The cash matters less than the signal: management is still pruning non-core consumer assets to concentrate capital and attention on AI and cloud, and gaming -- a business with its own content risk and regulatory history in China -- is now outside the perimeter. It also sets a mark for what buyers will pay for Alibaba's remaining non-core units ahead of earnings.

phases.headline: Alibaba to sell Lingxi Games in more than $2 billion deal, source says

events.whyItMatters: KKR has put an unsolicited ~$9bn proposal to UGI at $42.50 a share, a 21% premium to the $35.09 close before the report, for a group that bundles regulated Pennsylvania gas and electric utilities with midstream infrastructure, AmeriGas propane and European LPG distribution. It is the clearest sign yet that private capital is willing to pay up for regulated power and gas assets on the strength of data-center load growth. Nothing is agreed: the approach is WSJ-sourced, UGI's board has not said whether it will engage, and a rate-regulated utility take-private of this size faces state utility-commission review before anything closes.

phases.headline: KKR makes $9 billion takeover bid for energy distributor UGI, WSJ reports

events.whyItMatters: Madison Air pays $5.4bn of enterprise value ($5.0bn net of future tax savings) for Germany's ebm-papst, a fan and motor-systems maker with ~$2.8bn of expected 2026 revenue and more than 250m fans installed in about 40 countries -- 14.6x forecast 2026 adjusted EBITDA of ~$343m, or 10x including the $160m of run-rate synergies targeted by year three. It roughly doubles the addressable market and buys direct exposure to data-center cooling, but it is funded with cash plus new debt and equity behind UniCredit and Wells Fargo commitments, so a company that listed recently is levering up for a target larger than its own revenue base -- and the shares fell on the news.

phases.headline: Madison Air to Acquire ebm-papst, Expanding Return on Air Capabilities and Accelerating Durable Growth in Air Quality Solutions

events.whyItMatters: Francisco Partners takes patient-engagement software maker Weave private for about $650m at $7.40 a share in cash, a 34% premium to the August 17 unaffected close and unanimously approved by the board. The number that matters is the one it is measured against: Weave listed at roughly a $1.5bn valuation less than five years ago, so holders are being cashed out at well under half the IPO mark. It is another sub-scale listed SaaS name concluding that the public market will not fund the AI build-out its 40,000 healthcare practice locations expect; closing is guided to Q4 2026 subject to shareholder and regulatory approval.

phases.headline: Weave Announces Acquisition by Francisco Partners
phases.priceReaction: 34% premium to the August 17 unaffected close; among the NYSE's top gainers

events.whyItMatters: Deutsche Telekom buys 100% of Polish open-access fibre operator Fiberhost together with retail broadband and TV provider Inea from Macquarie Asset Management for about EUR1bn of enterprise value, adding a network passing more than 1.4m homes and over 300,000 customers. It converts T-Mobile Polska from a mobile-only operator into a convergent one in a market where fixed-line share has been the structural gap, and it is a rare case of Deutsche Telekom deploying capital into European fixed infrastructure rather than into buybacks. Closing is expected at the end of 2026, subject to Polish competition approval.

phases.headline: Deutsche Telekom to acquire Fiberhost and Inea from Macquarie Asset Management for c.1 billion EUR, thereby strengthening T-Mobile Polska's position in fixed broadband

events.whyItMatters: Marvell hands Google a warrant over 58.97m shares -- up to $12.2bn at a $206.58 strike, exercisable until August 2033 and worth roughly 7% of the company -- to anchor an expanded custom-silicon agreement signed on July 29 covering AI inference accelerators, storage, network and memory-interface controllers and near-memory compute for the TPU ecosystem. Only about 1.4m of the warrants vest in the first year; the rest unlock in tranches for every $500m of chips Google buys, so the dilution is paid for with volume rather than granted up front. It converts Marvell's most important custom-ASIC relationship into a contractual one with the customer on its own cap table -- and it does so at Broadcom's expense, which fell on the news.

phases.headline: Google Secures $12.2 Billion Share Purchase Right in Marvell AI Chip Deal

events.whyItMatters: Spanish agri-food cooperative Dcoop has taken the lead in a multi-bidder auction for Madrid-listed Deoleo, offering about EUR470m (~$545m) for a 57% stake in the world's largest olive-oil bottler, owner of Bertolli and Carbonell, in a combination reported to carry more than EUR2.2bn of turnover. The competition file is the catch: to clear US antitrust Dcoop would have to sell the Bertolli and Carapelli brands, so the winner of the whole would have to break it up immediately. Nothing is agreed -- Italy's Coricelli, Bonifiche Ferraresi and Newlat Food, France's Lesieur (Avril) and Australia's Cobram Estate Olives are all still circling -- but the process is reported to be in its final stages, with a deal possible as early as September.

phases.headline: Spain's Deoleo shares surge as olive oil maker draws takeover interest, with Dcoop leading a EUR470m ($545m) offer for a 57% stake
phases.priceReaction: +16% to a one-year high, its biggest daily gain since March 2022

events.whyItMatters: SK hynix's board has resolved to buy back and cancel 24.07m shares -- about 3.3% of the company, roughly KRW40trn (~$28.6bn) at the pre-vote KRW1,662,000 close -- in the largest treasury-share cancellation in the history of South Korean listed companies, purchasing on-market between August 20 and November 19 and retiring everything it buys. Alongside it management lifted the shareholder-return target from 'within 50%' to 'more than 50%' of cumulative 2025-27 free cash flow, explicitly on the view that the share price understates intrinsic value. Coming weeks after a KRW54trn commitment to two new fabs, it says the HBM upcycle is now generating enough cash to fund the capacity build and a record retirement at the same time -- which only holds if memory pricing does.

phases.headline: SK hynix Accelerates 40 Trillion won Share Repurchase and Cancellation Program, Pursues Shareholder Return Expansion to 'Over 50% of FCF'

events.whyItMatters: Charter has closed the $34.5bn Cox Communications merger after the California Public Utilities Commission cleared the last regulatory hurdle, and closed the all-stock Liberty Broadband acquisition the same day -- folding Cox's roughly 6m customers into Charter's 31m to create the largest US internet and video provider by subscribers, across 45 states, with the Spectrum lineup rolling into former Cox markets from mid-September. It ends a fifteen-month regulatory process and simplifies Charter's ownership structure in one step, but it also locks in the bet that scale is the answer to broadband subscriber losses: the synergies and the integration risk both now sit on the balance sheet, with no deal-break option left.

phases.headline: Charter Communications Closes $34.5 Billion Merger With Cox, Forming New Cable Giant

events.whyItMatters: Santander has completed the roughly $12.3bn purchase of Webster Financial announced in February, paying $48.75 in cash plus 2.0548 Santander ADSs per Webster share -- about $75.59, some 16% over Webster's 10-day VWAP and more than 2.0x tangible book. It is the largest US bank deal Santander has done and it changes what Santander US is: a relationship deposit base, a commercial banking franchise and Webster's Healthcare Financial Services platform now sit behind a business that has leaned on auto lending and wholesale funding. Webster leaves the NYSE, so the investment case is now Santander's -- whether a cheaper, stickier funding profile earns back a price paid at twice tangible book.

phases.headline: Santander completes acquisition of Webster in the U.S.

events.whyItMatters: Italy's Coricelli has countered with about EUR500m for Deoleo, topping the EUR470m Spanish cooperative Dcoop put on the table a day earlier (ole-dcoop-takeover-bid) and turning a lead into a live auction for the world's largest olive-oil bottler. Deoleo has now confirmed to the CNMV that both CVC (50.9%) and Alchemy (40.3%) are studying the sale of their stakes, so the whole register is in play rather than a single block, and Acesur is still circling alongside the two leaders. The strategic logic is consolidation ahead of a US market where Deoleo owns Bertolli and Carapelli -- which is also the catch, since an Italian buyer inherits the same brand-divestment problem any winner faces. Nothing is agreed and the process is reported to conclude as early as September.

phases.headline: Coricelli raises bid for Deoleo to 500 million

events.whyItMatters: Micron is committing $10bn over the next decade to Micron Research Labs, a Boise-anchored hub for foundational work on memory technologies, memory-compute architectures, packaging and future manufacturing, with construction starting in 2027 and satellite labs plus university partnerships funded alongside it. It is deliberately not product development, and it sits on top of the more than $250bn already committed to US manufacturing and R&D through 2035 -- so this is a memory maker using an AI cash windfall to buy optionality a decade out rather than returning it or adding another fab. The trade-off is explicit: roughly half a quarter's free cash flow a year spent where the payback cannot be modelled.

phases.headline: Micron Unveils Micron Research Labs, a U.S.-Based Long-Horizon Innovation Hub to Shape the Future of Memory and AI

events.whyItMatters: Monte dei Paschi's board has approved an all-share public exchange offer for Banco BPM worth EUR25.3bn at 1.567 new MPS shares per BPM share -- the larger of two simultaneous bids designed to make Siena too big to be swallowed by Intesa Sanpaolo's ~EUR30.5bn offer for MPS itself. Once MPS's proposed extraordinary distribution is counted the offer carries no premium to the 19 August prices, so BPM holders are being asked to swap a standalone franchise for roughly 37.2% of a self-built group rather than for cash. The acceptance period only runs from the first half of December 2026 to the first half of February 2027, which leaves a full quarter in which Intesa can respond and BPM's board can refuse -- and it converts a single-target takeover fight into a three-way contest for the shape of Italian banking.

phases.headline: Paschi Offers to Buy BPM, Banca Generali for EUR34 Billion

events.whyItMatters: The smaller leg of Monte dei Paschi's counter-offensive values Banca Generali at EUR8.72bn -- 6.958 new MPS shares apiece, an implied EUR74.284 a share and about a 10% premium, the only premium on the table across the two bids. Crucially the two offers are not conditionally linked, so this one can complete even if the Banco BPM leg fails, which makes it the cheaper insurance policy of the pair. For MPS it buys a fee-earning private-banking book to dilute a rate-sensitive lending balance sheet, and for Generali it would mean losing its asset-gathering distribution arm to a bank it does not control.

phases.headline: Monte dei Paschi board approves dual exchange offers for Banco Bpm and Banca Generali

events.whyItMatters: Broadcom is in talks with lenders to raise more than $60bn -- reported as potentially $70-80bn across a senior secured tranche and a roughly $30bn junior tranche -- to fund a special-purpose vehicle that buys Broadcom's own custom AI chips and leases them to Anthropic and potentially OpenAI, with Broadcom itself guaranteeing part of the senior debt. It scales the $35bn platform struck with Apollo and Blackstone in June toward the stated goal of over 20GW of compute for frontier labs by 2028. The significance is where the risk sits: Broadcom would be booking chip revenue against paper its own guarantee supports, which makes the customer's ability to service that debt, not the chip margin, the thing shareholders are underwriting. Talks are ongoing and the structure may change.

phases.headline: Broadcom seeks more than $60 billion in latest AI debt deal, Bloomberg News reports

events.whyItMatters: Arbutus intends to buy back up to $230m of stock through a modified Dutch auction at $5.00-$5.75 a share, opening on or about 24 August and expiring 29 September, funded from cash on hand -- essentially recycling the ~$178m non-contingent share of its Moderna patent settlement straight back to holders. At that price band the tender covers roughly a fifth of the company, so it is less a routine buyback than a statement that management values its own clinical pipeline below the cash the litigation produced. Holders who do not tender end up with a materially concentrated stake in a much smaller balance sheet.

phases.headline: Arbutus Announces Intent to Repurchase Up to US$230 Million of its Common Shares Through Modified "Dutch Auction" Tender Offer
